Day one.
A city street, a few kilometers inland.
The clocks say it is just past noon.
But the street lamps have switched on by themselves.
Their sensors only know that it is dark.
People stop on the pavement and stare up at a sky full of stars.
The walls and the asphalt still hold the warmth of the morning.
Without the Sun, that warmth would leak away into space, a degree or two every hour.
Shop owners would pull down their shutters.
One by one, people would head inside.
Behind every window, the heating would switch on.
Day three.
The temperature would drop below zero, and keep going.
Frost would spread over the cars, the benches and the roofs.
Down the street, a car would refuse to start.
Its driver would give up and walk home.
One week.
By now, the average temperature on Earth would be around minus seventeen degrees.
Then the water in the air would start to fall as snow.
Snow on the palm trees, in the middle of summer.
And this is only the first week.
